extracted.intended_audience: Grade 5 classroom teachers, professional development trainers, and district staff implementing the 6+1 Trait Writing model (also relevant to study designers and evaluators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for implementing and evaluating the 6+1 Trait Writing model for grade 5 instruction, including analytic scoring, classroom strategies, PD design, assessment administration, and study power/design considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing (ideas, organization, voice, word choice, sentence fluency, conventions, presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trait examined in exploratory analyses; treatment-group mean higher but difference not statistically significant for ideas in this study. Teachers are instructed to teach this trait via trait-based activities, lesson plans, and use of the analytic rubric to set objectives and assess growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This trait showed a statistically significant treatment effect in the study (effect sizes reported 0.117 to 0.144 for organization, voice, and word choice). Guidance includes use of graphic organizers and mode-specific structures (classroom strategy 6) to teach organization tied to prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice exhibited a statistically significant difference in this study. Teachers are encouraged to model writing, share 'work in progress', and engage students in justification and feedback activities to develop voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word choice — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word choice showed a statistically significant treatment effect in the study. Instructional strategies include extensive reading exposure and trait-focused mini-lessons to develop vocabulary and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence fluency (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence fluency — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as a trait for which treatment-group means were higher but not statistically significant in this study. Teachers are to use targeted lessons and rubric-driven practice to improve fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in trait-focused instruction and analytic scoring; differences for conventions were small in this study. Use rubric descriptors to teach and assess conventions explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (one of seven writing traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation — listed as one of the seven traits of effective writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the seven-trait analytic framework; teachers plan lessons and activities that address presentation alongside other traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic scoring rubric / scoring guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of analytic scoring rubrics used to assess the seven traits and to provide effective teacher feedback to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubrics provide indicators and language used to score and justify scores, support formative feedback, student self-assessment, and monitoring growth. Training involves group practice scoring sample papers, discussing justifications, and aligning lesson objectives with rubric rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 1: Teach students the language they need to speak and think like writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach students the language of the traits: rewriting the rubric, teaching vocabulary, and using rubrics to explain each indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplished by rewriting rubrics in student-friendly language and integrating trait vocabulary into lessons so students can explain and self-assess their writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 2: Read, score, and justify (RSJ) on anonymous sample papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Have students score model/anonymous papers as a group and justify the score using the rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the language of the rubric and scoring consistency; used in group practice during PD and classroom activities to build shared understanding of trait indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 3: Practice focused revision steps on weak papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a weak paper and revise it as a group, working with a partner or small group on an anonymous weak paper, revising for one trait/descriptor at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the writing process and makes revision concrete by focusing on a single trait or descriptor per revision cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 4: Model writing alongside students ('Model writing right now!')
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher writes with students, shares 'work in progress', asks students for revising feedback and allows them to score or revise teacher's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates writing as a craft, encourages risk-taking, and provides a live example for scoring and revision activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 5: Expose students to a wide variety of reading materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Read widely (printed material of all kinds) to illustrate strengths and weaknesses in writing and expose students to the five modes of writing and varied materials (menus, directions, greeting cards, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad reading supports understanding of modes, audience, and examples of trait strengths/weaknesses; use varied texts as mentor examples for trait instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 6: Practice structures of writing / modes using graphic organizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide graphic organizers for each writing mode to give students a 'skeleton' structure for organizing content appropriate to mode and prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic organizers help students construct pieces that enrich, clarify, and organize writing; tie organizers to MC*RAFTS prompts and mode-specific mini-lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 7: Use effective writing prompts (MC*RAFTS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MC*RAFTS prompts (Mode, Context * Role, Audience, Format, Topic, Strong verb) to create explicit writing prompts that encourage varied modes and higher-order responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MC*RAFTS builds on RAFT technique; 'S' (strong verb) clarifies the mode and cognitive demand; prompts should connect to other content areas and be used with graphic organizers (strategy 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 8: Set goals and monitor progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach students to set writing goals and continuously help them monitor progress using analytic rubrics for self-assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular monitoring results in timely, meaningful feedback and supports measurable student growth; students use rubrics to set objectives and track improvement by trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 9: Organize activities and mini-lessons by trait
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave focused trait skill lessons into the curriculum and use an index of lessons organized trait-by-trait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps teachers organize resources and provides a structured approach (text/manual) for yearlong trait instruction; mini-lessons target specific rubric indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Strategy 10: Plan and implement the traits using planning charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use planning charts to decide where traits fit in the year, break down rubric rows into student objectives, and plan trait units so students receive instruction on each rubric expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once students understand expectations and can self-assess, writing should improve; planning charts support systematic instruction and alignment with rubric indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trait cycle of instruction (lesson planning steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-step planning cycle: (1) Use the 6+1 Trait rubric to write lesson plans for each trait; (2) Teach the trait language by rewriting the rubric in student-friendly language; (3) Practice scoring sample papers and justify scores; (4) Develop trait-based activities and lesson plans; (5) Practice creating effective writing prompts and gather written products for formative assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cycle is explicitly used during PD planning sessions so teachers leave with formal lesson plans and a schedule for implementing trait instruction (e.g., focus on ideas and organization September–November).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development format and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended PD: a three-day summer institute followed by three full-day workshops during the year; PD provides participant manual, newsletters, and online technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary PD objectives: provide understanding of the traits, increase skills using analytic rubric, familiarize teachers with components of effective writing process, and acquaint teachers with the 10 classroom strategies. PD activities include group scoring, hands-on practice, modeling lessons, and planning time to create lesson plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop agenda items (one-day follow-up workshops)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-up workshop agenda: introduction/warm-up; group discussion of successes/challenges; review of 6+1 model (seven traits, student writing process, 10 strategies, trait cycle); review analytic rubric and practice scoring; model trait cycle use; plan lessons and activities; closure and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops emphasize troubleshooting, focused practice on specific traits, scoring practice with discussion of rationale, and time to plan upcoming classroom activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online support and exemplar comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Online resources provide sample grade 5 student papers illustrating traits, opportunities to practice scoring and compare to expert raters, suggested books, and technical assistance via email/phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online exemplars to calibrate scoring, support teacher practice between workshops, and supplement printed PD materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test administration: timing and proctoring guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing assessments are completed over three consecutive days during 45–50 minute uninterrupted periods; teachers give brief instructions but students write on their own without peer or teacher assistance in planning, drafting, revising, or editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers may reread the prompt to individual students but must not offer content suggestions or proofread; allow students to proceed at their own pace; provide quiet activities for early finishers so they do not disturb others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test administration: allowed resources and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students may use a dictionary and thesaurus normally available in school for definitions, usage, or spelling. Students may NOT use local handouts beyond word definitions, reference sources (textbooks, encyclopedias), peer editing, or computers (unless specified in IEP/504).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodations specified in a student's IEP or 504 plan are allowed (including computer/word processor if specified). Do not permit external resources that go beyond word-level help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test administration: logistical and materials procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Before assessment, ensure each student has a Writing Booklet with the correct code and name; read boxed directions verbatim; instruct students not to write names in certain places and that booklets will be sent for scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the explicit step-by-step administration script (Day 1 planning, rough draft steps) to preserve standardization; record missing booklet assignments on classroom roster and match codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research design metric: power analysis, ICC, and minimum detectable effect (MDE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power analysis uses intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and effect of covariates (R2_L2) to estimate required sample sizes for specified minimum detectable effect sizes (MDE) at power = 0.8. Example reported unconditional ICC ≈ 0.14, conditional ICC ≈ 0.079, R2_L2 = 0.428; sample-size/MDE table provided (e.g., 54 schools needed for MDE ≈ 0.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (number of schools, students per school, students per teacher, alpha level) determine MDE. Recalculation indicated MDEs of 0.25 (15 students/school), 0.23 (20 students), 0.22 (30 students) for 74 schools; retrospective MDES reported for various analyses and scales.
